'''Wen-Ch'ing (Winnie) Li''' ({{lang-zh|c=李文卿}}; born December 25, 1948) is a Taiwanese-American mathematician and a Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref name="distinguished">[http://science.psu.edu/news-and-events/2012-news/Li1-2012 Winnie Li Named Distinguished Professor], [[Pennsylvania State University]], 30 January 2012, retrieved 2013-02-02.</ref> She is a [[number theorist]], with research focusing on the theory of [[automorphic forms]] and applications of [[number theory]] to [[coding theory]] and [[spectral graph theory]]. In particular, she has applied her research results in automorphic forms and number theory to construct efficient communication networks called [[Ramanujan graphs]] and Ramanujan complexes.

==Professional career==
Li graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in mathematics in 1970.<ref name="distinguished"/><ref name="nthu"/> As an undergraduate, she was a classmate of mathematicians [[Fan Chung]], [[Sun-Yung Alice Chang]] and [[Jang-Mei Wu]].<ref>[http://community.sciencecareers.org/myscinet/partners/awm/2009/01/fan-chung-graham.php Fan Chung Graham], Association for Women in Mathematics, retrieved 2013-02-02.</ref> She then earned her [[Ph.D]]. in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1974, under the supervision of [[Andrew Ogg]].<ref name="distinguished"/><ref name="nthu"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=32309|name=Wen-Ching Winnie Li}}</ref> 

Before joining faculty of Pennsylvania State University in 1979, she was a Benjamin Pierce assistant professor at [[Harvard University]] for 3.5 years from 1974 to 1977, and a tenure-track assistant professor at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] from 1978 to 1979.<ref name="distinguished" /><ref name="nthu" /> She was also the director of the National Center of Theoretical Sciences in [[Taiwan]] from 2009 to 2014.<ref name="distinguished" /><ref name="nthu">[http://math.cts.nthu.edu.tw/Mathematics/english/academic_c/WLi-eng.html Staff biography] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130610005534/http://math.cts.nthu.edu.tw/Mathematics/english/academic_c/WLi-eng.html |date=2013-06-10 }}, National Center of Theoretical Sciences, retrieved 2013-02-02.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2010, Li was the winner of the [[Chern Prize (ICCM)|Chern Prize]], given every three years to an outstanding Chinese mathematician.<ref>[http://science.psu.edu/news-and-events/2011-news/Li1-2011 Wen Ching Li Awarded the 2010 Chern Prize in Mathematics], [[Pennsylvania State University]], 30 January 2012, retrieved 2013-02-02.</ref> In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref> She was chosen to give the 2015 [[Noether Lecture]].<ref>[https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/wen-ching-winnie-li “Modular Forms for Congruence and Noncongruence Subgroups”]</ref>
